extractor_notes: Runtime is stated as '13 min 42 s'. The schema accepts an integer only, so runtime_minutes is recorded as 13; the precise stated runtime is 13 minutes 42 seconds. The input describes two distinct pieces of material under one title: the full music video (13 min 42 s, slot 22:15) and a 30-second trailer cut from it (shown in a 15:00 break). The schema has one content_type for the asset, so it is set to music_video for the main work; observations o8 to o10 are the trailer's events and are marked as such in what_happens and descriptors, because the schema has no field linking an observation to a particular transmission or to a particular cut. That link is therefore not expressible: o1 to o7 belong to t1 and o8 to o10 to t2. The trailer's timecodes ('00:05', '00:18') are elapsed times within the 30-second trailer and are preserved exactly as given, which means they collide numerically with music-video timecodes while referring to a different piece of material; o3/o4 and o8/o9 both read '00:05' for this reason. Timecodes throughout are given to the minute (HH:MM) rather than HH:MM:SS and the lists are labelled 'indicative'; they are not padded or estimated. 'CERTIFICATE: none' is recorded as an empty existing_certificates array. 'COUNTRIES: UK, FR' is ambiguous: it may mean territories of transmission, countries of production or rights territories; it is not used for production_origin, which is left not_stated. The NOTE about the opening disclaimer is recorded as observation o7 because it is on-screen content; it has no timecode of its own beyond 'opens the work', and I cannot tell from the input whether the disclaimer is included in the trailer. The disclaimer and the content of the work sit in some tension as evidence: the work states it does not endorse belief in the occult while depicting supernatural events; both are recorded without reconciling them. Occult_paranormal is used for the werewolf transformation, the risen corpses, the non-human eyes and the disclaimer because they are supernatural/occult-referring; fear_distress is recorded separately where the input supplies detail about how the material is presented (sustained close-up, decayed faces in detail, pursuit and cornering). o2 is medium confidence because the input states the presentational detail but says nothing about intended or likely effect on a viewer. 'is_news_or_current_affairs' is 'no' on the basis of the stated descriptor 'music video'. 'is_made_primarily_for_children' is not_stated: the input says nothing about intended audience.
